newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-OLD FIRM HOPE TO SHOW QUALITY GAP AGAINST BOTTOM TWO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-OLD FIRM HOPE TO SHOW QUALITY GAP AGAINST BOTTOM TWO.

text.p: The quality gap between big and small in the Spanish league should be shown in stark contrast as Real Madrid and Barcelona -- lying first and second respectively -- take on the bottom two clubs in weekend fixtures.

The visit of mighty Real to struggling Extremadura is a huge event in the remote rural town of Almendralejo, whose 25,000 inhabitants would fit more than four times into Real's Santiago Bernabeu stadium.

Even bigger than the Bernabeu is Barcelona's vast Camp Nou ground, where fans are licking their lips at the prospect of a goal avalanche against bottom-but-one Hercules in a televised game which has been put back to Monday.
Anything less than a massacre could anger one of Europe's most demanding crowds.
Barca supporters booed their star-studded team when Extremadura left the Camp Nou with only a 3-0 defeat two months ago.
Since then Barcelona have lost their way, giving up an unbeaten record in successive defeats at Athletic Bilbao and then going down 2-0 in the old firm game against Real Madrid.
But Bobby Robson's side managed a late winner at third-placed Deportivo Coruna last week when Brazilian prodigy Ronaldo returned to his best form.

Away games await both Deportivo, who are three points off the pace, and Betis, a further point back, giving both Real and Barcelona a chance to put some distance between themselves and the chasing group.
For Real, who cross the Spanish capital to face reigning champions Atletico the following weekend, a win on Sunday is particularly important.
Manager Fabio Capello may face the game without energetic Brazilian full-back Roberto Carlos, who went down with 'flu and missed Thursday's 2-1 victory over Valladolid in the Spanish Cup.
But Real have been boosted by the signing of AC Milan defender Christian Panucci.
Panucci's fee, thought to be as much as 750 million pesetas ($5.73 million), is nearly as large as Extremadura's budget for the entire season.

The annual salary of Real striker Predrag Mijatovic -- thought to be around 250 million pesetas ($1.91 million) -- is more than 60 times that of Extremadura midfielder Ito Alvarez, who earns the league minimum wage of four million pestas ($30,500).
Despite just one win in 18 games, the Extremadura club and fans are relishing their once-in-a-lifetime brush with the high life and have even offered to renew the contract of coach Josu Ortuondo.
Meanwhile club president Pedro Nieto has picked up some of the tricks of first division old-timers like Jesus Gil and regularly blasts referees for poor decisions.
The match, not surprisingly, is a sell-out which will generate club-record takings for Extremadura's first game with Real Madrid since their meeting in the Spanish Cup in 1959.
Two months before winning their fourth successive European Cup, Real's Alfredo di Stefano and company waltzed to a 5-0 win.
